chassis.note: The product page prints "13.34 cm x 8.46 cm x 2.42 cm (5.25 in x 3.33 in x 0.95 in)" labelled L x W x D. The line art shows the two ends as the wide faces, so 133.4 is the depth of the unit, 84.6 the width of each end and 24.2 its height; the page's D is read as the thickness. The page prints one size for all three models.

colour.note: The photograph shows a black body (16, 16, 16 read off the top) and a bright metal jack shield. The legends ETHERNET, RESET and 9-30V DC 525mA MAX are white. LINK and PWR are green and ACT and READY are yellow. Green about #37855d and yellow about #d9d965 are the medians of the brightest saturated pixels of each word in the 682 px photograph: estimates.

front-layout.note: From the front line art: the Ethernet jack 7.4 from the left, the first lamp pair at 27.2, a slot 11.6 wide from 31.6, a small square button at 48.7, the second lamp pair at 61.8 and the power jack at 71.7 (centres). The legends are not on this face; the photograph prints them on the top.

gate-1.note: Each line-art end is read at its own scale across, from the outline of the face (0.495 mm per pixel on the front, 0.460 on the back), and down from the face's own height. The line art is a small picture whose proportions are not exact (the front outline is 10 per cent taller in proportion than the stated size), so every position is good to about 2 mm.

lamps.note: The page lists the lamps "Link, activity, power, status". The photograph prints LINK and ACT over the first pair and PWR and READY over the second. The quick start guide gives states for its Power, Link, 10/100, ACT and COL lamps, under names that differ from the photograph's legends, and no colour; so each lamp has on and off only.

ports.note: The product page lists "4 RS-232 RJ-45; up to 230 kbps throughput; signal support for TXD, RXD, RTS, CTS, DTR, DSR, DCD" and "1 RJ-45 10/100 Mbps 10/100Base-T (auto-sensing)". The quick start guide, page 1, says "PortServer TS products use an RJ-45 10-wire jack (female)", so each serial jack is the ten-position jack.

power.note: The product page prints "9-30 VDC" as the input, a supply of "12 VDC / 1.5 A max out" and "Typical: 4 W; Max: 6 W" consumed. The line art and the quick start guide show a locking barrel jack. The photograph prints "9-30V DC 525mA MAX" beside the jack. The photograph also shows a terminal-block connector where the line art shows the barrel; the barrel is drawn, and the difference is listed among the gaps.

rear-layout.note: From the back line art: the serial jacks stand in one row, each opening 16.0 wide on a 16.0 pitch from 7.4, with 13.2 free at the right. The 1-port, 2-port and 4-port brackets in the drawing end at the first, second and fourth jack, so the PortServer TS 4 fills all four. The words RJ-45 Serial are printed under the jacks in the drawing.

sources.note: Digi PortServer TS product page (digi.com, read 2026-11-05): ports, power, size, weight, part numbers and accessories. Digi's PortServer TS family line art, front and back (181 x 110 and 209 x 110 px): the position of every jack, lamp, slot and button, as drawing. Digi's PortServer TS family quick start guide (90000687-88), page 1: the serial jack is a ten-wire RJ-45, and page 2: the locking power connector with its centre pin positive. One angled photograph of the PortServer TS 1: the black body and the legends printed on the top. No data sheet or user guide is held; the data sheet is behind a form on the maker's site and the user guide is a link to a document not held.

top-layout.note: From the angled photograph of the PortServer TS 1: the logo at the rear left, the wordmark PORTSERVER and TS near the front edge and, on the edge itself, the legends ETHERNET, LINK, ACT, RESET, PWR, READY and 9-30V DC 525mA MAX. The photograph is in perspective, so the legends take the x of the part each one labels in the line art, and the wordmark is placed to about 5 mm.
